slides.title: What we'll do in this session
slides.content: There's nothing to revise and nothing to get wrong today. This is your very first session on your Digital or Media course — about 55–60 minutes to settle in, meet the people you'll work with, and understand what this year asks of you.

exercise.prompt: Which best describes the purpose of today's Module A session?
options: Pass an entrance test for the course
Settle in, meet people and understand what the year asks of you
Choose your modules for the year
exercise.answer: Settle in, meet people and understand what the year asks of you

slides.title: The session in six steps
slides.content: Six things will happen today: meet your group, meet your teachers, your study programme, your timetable & Pro Portal, support at college, and enrichment & Freshers.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Belonging Matters'? Select all that apply.
options: You know people in your group
You have staff you can approach
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Belonging Matters.

slides.title: Belonging is the point
slides.content: Belonging is the single biggest factor in whether students stay, attend and succeed. Knowing even a couple of friendly faces makes everything that follows feel easier. You will not click with everyone — that's normal. The goal today is that no one feels alone.

exercise.prompt: According to the deck, what is the single biggest factor in whether students stay, attend and succeed?
exercise.explanation: Belonging is the single biggest factor in whether students stay, attend and succeed.

slides.title: Your study programme
slides.content: Your study programme is more than just lessons. It has four parts: your Digital or Media qualification (the core course — coursework, portfolio and final projects), English & maths (if you haven't yet achieved these), work-related learning (industry placements, live briefs and real creative experience — for T-Level students this is mandatory), and tutorial & personal development time.

exercise.prompt: Which of these are part of your study programme? Select all that apply.
options: English & maths (if you haven't yet achieved them)

slides.title: Timetable & Pro Portal — the golden rule
slides.content: Pro Portal is your digital home at college: your timetable, messages from teachers, attendance, progress and links to learning and services. The golden rule is to check Pro Portal every morning before you set off — it's the first place any room or timetable changes appear.

exercise.prompt: Fill in the blank: check your Pro Portal every ____ before you set off.
exercise.template: Check your Pro Portal every ____ before you set off.
exercise.explanation: Check your Pro Portal every morning before you set off.

slides.title: You're not on your own
slides.content: Everyone needs help sometimes — it's a sign of sense, not weakness. There are four kinds of support at college: learning support (studies, extra needs, exam access), wellbeing & mental health (someone to talk to if you're struggling, stressed or low), money & practical help (bursary, travel, equipment), and careers & next steps (jobs, university, apprenticeships and your future).

exercise.prompt: Which kind of college support covers bursary, travel and equipment?
exercise.explanation: Money & practical help covers bursary, travel, equipment and other practical support.

slides.title: More than your course
slides.content: College is also where you try things, meet people and build a life outside lessons. The ESC enrichment programme is the clubs, sports, societies and activities available this year. Your Freshers Fair runs in the next couple of weeks — stalls, clubs, freebies and a chance to sign up. Go along, even if you go with one new friend from today.

exercise.prompt: When does your Freshers Fair happen, according to the deck?
options: In the next couple of weeks
exercise.explanation: In the next couple of weeks your campus runs a Freshers Fair.

slides.title: What's next
slides.content: Over the next three weeks you'll have more short induction sessions — staying safe, looking after yourself, and getting ready for your future. None of them are tests; they're here to help you settle and succeed.

exercise.prompt: How does the deck describe the induction sessions coming up over the next three weeks?
options: They are mocks of your final exams
They are short, supportive sessions, not tests
exercise.explanation: None of them are tests. They're here to help you settle and succeed.
